site.name: Ohio-Colorado Smelting & Refining Co. Smokestack / Smeltertown
overview: The Ohio-Colorado Smelting and Refining Company operated a major smelting complex at Smeltertown near Salida from 1902 to 1920. Its surviving 365-foot smokestack, completed in 1917, remains a prominent monument to the Upper Arkansas Valley's mining and ore-processing industry.

timeline.text: The Ohio-Colorado Smelting and Refining Company began operating its smelter near Salida, using the area's railroad connections to receive ores and fuel from regional mining districts.
Construction of the surviving tall smokestack began in 1916 and was completed in 1917 to disperse smelter fumes farther from surrounding farms and communities.
The Ohio-Colorado smelter closed, leaving the tall stack as the most visible surviving feature of the former industrial complex.
The smokestack was listed in the National Register of Historic Places as an important reminder of the region's mining industry and workers.

moreHistory: A 1916 mining-industry paper described the Salida plant as an 80-acre smelting complex beside the Arkansas River, positioned to use the Denver & Rio Grande railroad network serving the San Juan, Crested Butte, Monarch, and Garfield mining areas.
The surviving stack is built of brick and tile and rises 365 feet. Local preservation efforts saved it from demolition in the 1970s, and the Salida Museum Association became its steward.
